key_insight: A physics-informed token transformer (PITT) combines symbolic PDE tokenization, learned operators, and exact shock-jump physics to accurately evolve nonlinear balance-law solutions with moving and stationary discontinuities.
engineering_relevance: The method improves shock tracking and steady-state preservation for hyperbolic flow problems with geometric effects, making it promising for CFD settings where front location and long-time stability matter.
method: Tokenize the governing equation and encode it with a Fourier neural operator.
Advance leading discontinuities using the explicit Rankine–Hugoniot shock condition.
Use a learned correction term to reconstruct smooth regions, rarefactions, and finite-resolution effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on moving shocks, stationary shocks, rarefaction waves, and long-time perturbed steady states, with comparisons against a standard high-order finite-volume method and a Burgers-limit study.
watch_item: Performance depends on having an explicit shock law and explicit steady-state structure, so extension to systems or problems without known analytic jump conditions may be harder.
paper_title: Physics-informed token transformer methodology for nonlinear balance laws. I. Schwarzschild--Burgers fluid flows
